title: Officers won't be charged in death of 17-year-old
article: Ontario police officers were legally justified in shooting a 17-year-old to death earlier this summer and will not face charges, say investigators.

Geronimo Fobister, 17, was killed Aug. 27 during a stand-off with Ontario Provincial Police officers, who had tracked him down to a trail in a heavily wooded area near his home on the Grassy Narrows First Nation.
Fobister was wanted in an incident earlier that day in which a community resident was allegedly shot at by two men, said investigators.
After an eight-week investigation, an independent agency assigned to look into the shooting ruled it was justified.
"I find the officers' accounts are inherently plausible, consistent with each other, and consistent with the rest of the evidence," unit director John Sutherland said in a news release.
